mountain_clansmen.name: Mountain Clansmen
mountain_clansmen.description: A composite warband of three thousand Vale mountain tribesman: Stone Crows, Black Ears, Moon Brothers, and Burned Men, press-ganged into Lannister service by Tyrion's promises of steel and plunder. They are individually ferocious fighters, hardened by lives of inter-clan raiding in the high passes, lightly armoured but aggressive beyond reckoning. Tyrion commands them in name; in practice each clan chief leads his own warband, and the whole formation coheres through momentum and savagery rather than discipline. Tywin places them in the van as an expendable shock screen — their aggression is real, but they are not expected to hold a line.
strengths: Devastating initial charge: individually skilled fighters who hit hard in the first rush
High morale derived from personal pride and clan honour — they do not shame themselves before enemies
Excellent in broken or rugged ground where their skirmishing style is effective
Unpredictable and terrifying; their appearance and battle-cries unsettle inexperienced levies
weaknesses: Near-zero unit cohesion — each clan fights for itself; coordinated maneuver is impossible
No shields or heavy armour; they cannot endure sustained missile fire or hold a defensive line
If the charge stalls and casualties mount, morale collapses rapidly — they are not built to absorb punishment
Subject to clan rivalry: individual chiefs may pursue personal glory over the tactical mission
mountain_clansmen.morale_notes: High baseline morale from personal pride, but brittle under sustained pressure. A single bloody repulse can cause the entire formation to dissolve into individual bands. Tyrion's personal influence is limited; he survives this battle largely through luck and Shagga's affection for him.
mountain_clansmen.historical_context: In A Game of Thrones, Tyrion leads the mountain clans at the Green Fork under his father's orders — a deliberate slight from Tywin, who expects Tyrion to die in the van. The clans survive because Tywin's design works: the van absorbs the shock of the northern charge while the center and reserve horse deliver the decisive blow. Their role is to be sacrificed; the fact that they are not annihilated is almost incidental. Clan chiefs present: Shagga son of Dolf (Stone Crows), Timett son of Timett (Burned Men), Chella daughter of Cheyk (Black Ears), Conn son of Coratt (Moon Brothers).

lannister_vanguard.name: Vanguard Heavy Foot
lannister_vanguard.description: A combined body of roughly thirty-five hundred Lannister men-at-arms, household knights fighting dismounted, and veteran sellswords, all operating under the savage command of Ser Gregor Clegane. These are the real teeth of the Lannister van — disciplined, well-armoured, capable of holding a shield wall under pressure. Their role is to receive the northern charge, soak the initial shock, and hold long enough for the center to stabilize and the reserve horse to swing into position. Gregor leads from the front, and his personal presence — terrifying to friend and foe alike — holds the line when anyone else might break.
strengths: Disciplined heavy infantry capable of holding a shield wall under serious pressure
Gregor Clegane's personal command provides an exceptional morale anchor and shock bonus
Well-equipped; they can absorb casualties better than the levies to their flank
Excellent at grinding attrition combat — they are built to bleed the northern spears
weaknesses: Tired from sustained marching before the battle; they lack the fresh-legs edge
Fighting on open ground that slightly favours the northern offensive formation
If Gregor is incapacitated the leadership vacuum causes rapid cohesion loss
Dependent on the center men-at-arms to their rear — if the center does not advance in support, the van is isolated
lannister_vanguard.morale_notes: Steady baseline morale — professional soldiers who know the score. Gregor's presence keeps them fighting through situations that would break most units. However, they have absorbed a night march and are not at their physical peak.
lannister_vanguard.historical_context: Ser Gregor Clegane personally leads the Lannister vanguard. His reputation as the most feared knight in Westeros is relevant here — his presence in the line is a genuine force multiplier. The vanguard's purpose is to pin Roose Bolton's infantry in place while Tywin's reserve cavalry delivers the decisive stroke from the ridge.

western_levy.name: Western Levy Spears
western_levy.description: Conscript spearmen and billmen raised from the smallfolk of the westerlands — numerically significant but of limited military value. They are poorly trained, lightly armoured, and their morale is fragile. Tywin places them on the weaker flank of the van deliberately: if the northern attack focuses here, the levies will bend and perhaps break, but that bending is part of the plan — it channels northern momentum toward the better-positioned center and draws their strength onto ground where the reserve horse can exploit.
strengths: Numerous — they take up flank space and force the northern commander to commit units against them
Cheap and expendable; their loss does not significantly weaken Tywin's quality core
Spear formation provides some passive resistance against cavalry charges
weaknesses: Wavering morale — they will break under hard pressure without strong leadership nearby
Tired from the march; physically and psychologically at a low point
Limited fighting quality; experienced northern foot will cut through them given opportunity
No initiative capacity — they hold or they run, no nuanced tactical response
western_levy.morale_notes: Wavering at the outset. These men are not soldiers by choice. A significant early setback — taking heavy archery fire, losing men to the northern charge — may trigger a rout that exposes the Lannister left. Tywin has calculated this risk and positioned accordingly, but the levy rout must not happen too early.
western_levy.historical_context: The western levies represent the weakest part of Tywin's force, deliberately deployed where they can absorb punishment without compromising the quality core. In the actual battle, the left wing 'unexpectedly fought well' per Tyrion's later recollection, but this may be a Tyrion POV underestimation rather than historical record.

lannister_center.name: Center Men-at-Arms
lannister_center.description: The backbone of Tywin's army: forty-five hundred disciplined Lannister men-at-arms organized in the main battle under Ser Kevan Lannister's steady command. These are the finest heavy infantry in the westerlands — veterans of House Lannister's decades of dominance, well-supplied and well-led. Their role is to hold the center with absolute firmness, absorb any breakthrough from the van, counter-push when the northern attack begins to exhaust itself, and create the conditions for the reserve horse to deliver the killing blow. Kevan is methodical, reliable, and does not panic.
strengths: The highest-quality heavy infantry on the field — disciplined, well-equipped, veteran
Kevan Lannister's reliable command: no tactical errors, no loss of nerve
Positioned in the center where they can influence every threatened sector
Fresh enough at battle-start to mount a sustained counter-push after absorbing the northern assault
Can effectively anchor flanking units left and right
weaknesses: Heavy infantry is slower to maneuver than the cavalry wings; committed to their sector
If the van collapses catastrophically before the center engages, they absorb the impact without buffer
The weight of the entire Lannister defensive plan rests on them not breaking — a single serious setback cracks the whole formation
lannister_center.morale_notes: High morale. Kevan's steadiness is infectious. These men have confidence in their commander, their equipment, and their numbers. They will not break easily.
lannister_center.historical_context: Ser Kevan Lannister commands the main battle and is Tywin's most trusted operational subordinate. At the Green Fork he performs his role flawlessly — the center holds, the van absorbs the charge, and Tywin's reserve delivers the decision from the ridge.

lannister_archers.name: Crossbows & Archers
lannister_archers.description: Two thousand crossbowmen and composite archers positioned on the forward slope of Tywin's Ridge, providing fire support over the heads of the van into the advancing northern formation. The crossbow is Tywin's preferred ranged weapon — slower to reload than a longbow but punching through armor at useful ranges. These men fire in ordered volleys, directed by Ser Forley Prester, and can inflict significant early casualties on the northern spears before contact. Their position on the ridge gives them a slight elevation advantage. They are, however, vulnerable if the northern line breaks through to their position.
strengths: Strong pre-contact fire suppression: volleys into advancing northern formations reduce their strength before engagement
Elevation bonus from the ridge improves range and accuracy
Crossbows punch through northern mail and padded armor effectively
Can continue firing into flanks of combats in progress once the lines engage
weaknesses: Extremely vulnerable to melee combat; if the northern breakthrough reaches the ridge, they are nearly defenseless
Limited mobility — repositioning while under attack is very slow
Fire support effectiveness drops once the lines intermingle, risking friendly fire on the van
lannister_archers.morale_notes: Steady and professional. These are trained ranged troops who believe in their position and their orders. They do not expect to be tested in melee.
lannister_archers.historical_context: Tywin's positioning of his crossbows on the ridge slope is a deliberate force-multiplier. They represent early attrition that will reduce the northern attack's momentum before it even reaches the van. In the battle they contribute to the general Lannister fire superiority.

lannister_right_horse.name: Right Wing Heavy Horse
lannister_right_horse.description: Twenty-five hundred western knights and lancers under Ser Addam Marbrand's aggressive command, positioned on the firm, dry eastern ground — the ideal cavalry maneuver space of the battle. Marbrand is one of Tywin's best cavalry officers: fast, decisive, and capable of reading terrain. His role is to hold the eastern flank, screen against any northern cavalry probe through the East Woods, and exploit any opportunity to swing wide and hit the northern flank in coordination with the reserve's central charge. Addam's outriders had been probing the northern advance all morning, so he enters battle with solid tactical intelligence.
strengths: Heavy shock cavalry on ideal ground — open, firm, dry eastern field maximizes lance charge effectiveness
Addam Marbrand's aggressive competence makes him quick to exploit gaps or flanks
Can threaten to turn the entire northern left flank if their position weakens
Cavalry speed allows them to react to northern moves faster than infantry units
weaknesses: Committed to the eastern flank — cross-field maneuver to assist the west is slow
The East Woods opposite them provide the northern light horse with an ambush corridor
Northern White Harbor infantry, if they hold the east field, can disrupt the flank drive
lannister_right_horse.morale_notes: High morale — western knights with confidence in their commander, their horses, and their ground. These men expect to win.
lannister_right_horse.historical_context: Ser Addam Marbrand commanded the outriders before the battle, providing Tywin with intelligence about Bolton's night march. In the battle he commands the right-wing cavalry and is credited with helping drive the northern left flank against the river, contributing to the Lannister victory.

lannister_left_horse.name: Left Wing Horse
lannister_left_horse.description: Fifteen hundred mixed light and medium horse under Ser Lyle Crakehall's command, screening the western flank near the muddy ground beside the Green Fork. 'Strongboar' Crakehall is a competent but not exceptional cavalry officer. His horses are working in the most difficult terrain on the field — the ground near the Green Fork is soft and treacherous, which blunts their shock potential. Their role is purely screening: prevent the Cerwyn-Hornwood levies from wrapping the Lannister left flank, and tie down northern attention on the western side while the real action unfolds in the center.
strengths: Cavalry mobility gives them positional flexibility even in difficult ground
Their presence forces the northern commander to devote attention to the western flank
Can harry retreating northern units if the western line collapses
weaknesses: Muddy ground near the river significantly reduces cavalry effectiveness — slower, less shock
Lighter weight than the right-wing — they cannot punch through a determined northern defensive line
If the Cerwyn-Hornwood levies push aggressively, the soft ground limits Crakehall's counter-charge options
lannister_left_horse.morale_notes: Steady professional cavalry. They know their ground is difficult and do not expect to be decisive — they are screen troops and accept that role.
lannister_left_horse.historical_context: The western flank of the Lannister position is the softest part of Tywin's deployment, held deliberately to channel northern momentum toward the center. Crakehall's horse exist primarily to prevent a northern flanking envelopment, not to deliver a decisive blow.

tywins_reserve.name: Tywin's Reserve Heavy Horse
tywins_reserve.description: Twenty-five hundred of the finest heavy cavalry in Westeros — the premier western knights held back deliberately on Tywin's Ridge under the Lord of Casterly Rock's personal command. These men are fresh, superbly equipped, and psychologically prepared for the moment of decision. Tywin uses his reserve with cold, calculating patience: he watches the battle develop from his elevated position, allows the van to absorb the northern attack, waits for the moment the northern line is spent and their impetus exhausted, and then commits the hammer. 'The remnants of the Stark lines shattered like glass beneath the hammer of their charge.' This is the decisive blow Tywin has designed the entire battle to deliver.
strengths: The freshest and most powerful unit on the field — arriving at full strength into a battle where both sides are already spent
Tywin's personal command provides the highest possible quality of commitment timing — he will not rush this
Heavy cavalry shock on exhausted infantry is devastatingly effective
Elevated start position gives them momentum for the downhill charge
The psychological impact of this reserve's arrival — after the northern force has already absorbed the van — is catastrophic for northern morale
weaknesses: Tywin must hold them until the right moment — committing too early wastes the tactical advantage
If the northern infantry forms up pike-hedge specifically to receive cavalry, effectiveness is reduced
The ridge-to-van approach, though downhill, crosses several contested nodes
tywins_reserve.morale_notes: Fanatic-adjacent: these knights ride for the richest lord in Westeros, at the moment they have been trained and waited for. Their morale is as high as any unit on the field.
tywins_reserve.historical_context: Tywin's reserve was the decisive element at the Green Fork. His cold patience in waiting for the right moment — while Tyrion's mountain clans and the vanguard foot were taking casualties — then unleashing the heavy horse is exactly how he intended to fight. The quote 'shattered like glass beneath the hammer of their charge' (from Tyrion's later reflection) describes the effect of this reserve on the already-spent northern infantry.

northern_vanguard.name: Northern Vanguard Spears
northern_vanguard.description: Four thousand northern foot — hardy spearmen and axemen from across the northern bannermen — forming the tip of Bolton's assault. These are the men who marched through the night down the Kingsroad, arriving before dawn in hopes of catching the Lannisters unprepared. They are tired from the forced march but fuelled by northern stubbornness and the grim sense that this fight, whatever its outcome, is part of Robb's larger plan. Ser Helman Tallhart commands the van. The northern spear is typically shorter and heavier than southern weapons, designed for close-quarters fighting in the brutal northern tradition.
strengths: Hardy, experienced fighters who are accustomed to hard conditions — cold, fatigue, and discomfort do not break them as easily as southern troops
Numerous — they can sustain meaningful casualties and keep fighting
Attacking formation: they have the psychological momentum of the advance
Northern spear-and-axe combination effective in the grinding center fight
weaknesses: Tired from the all-night forced march — their physical edge is significantly reduced
Attacking across the creek obstacle at the field's center causes disorder before contact
Facing the Lannister heavy foot and Gregor Clegane's van — a difficult match-up even fresh
No cavalry support — Robb took nearly all the horse west; the van cannot be rescued or exploited by mounted reserves
northern_vanguard.morale_notes: Steady but not inspired. They march to pin Tywin, knowing the strategic success depends on Robb elsewhere. This is sacrificial work and they know it. Tallhart keeps them moving forward through sheer grim duty.
northern_vanguard.historical_context: Helman Tallhart commands the northern van at the Green Fork. His men form the first wave against the Lannister position. The all-night march gives them the element of surprise in timing but costs them significantly in physical readiness. The battle goes badly but Bolton retreats in good order — Tallhart's van buys time even in defeat.

dreadfort_foot.name: Dreadfort Foot
dreadfort_foot.description: Three thousand of Roose Bolton's own household troops and bannermen from the Dreadfort and its environs — the most disciplined, battle-hardened force in the northern army. Bolton holds them back deliberately throughout the engagement, spending the levies and the van while preserving his own men. The Dreadfort soldiers are cold, controlled, and utterly loyal to their pale-eyed lord. They are the northern version of Tywin's reserve in concept, though Bolton's purpose is different: not the decisive blow, but the orderly retreat that preserves his force for future use. Bolton is not playing to win this battle; he is playing to survive it in good order while costing Tywin's army as much as possible.
strengths: The best-quality infantry in the northern force — disciplined, steady, and experienced
Bolton's cautious command keeps them from being wasted on lost positions
Their fresh state (Steady, not Tired) gives them meaningful physical advantage in any late-battle engagement
Can serve as a rearguard to cover the withdrawal if the line breaks
weaknesses: Bolton's deliberate restraint means they may not be committed even when they could have shifted the battle — he is saving them for what comes next
Isolated behind the main engagement — they must move through contested ground to reinforce
Their cold, controlled culture means they lack the aggressive shock of the van's attack formations
dreadfort_foot.morale_notes: Steady and controlled. The Dreadfort soldiers mirror their lord — they do not break, they do not panic, and they do not waste themselves. This is both their great strength and, from Robb's perspective, their great frustration.
dreadfort_foot.historical_context: Roose Bolton's management of his own troops at the Green Fork is widely noted. He preserved the Dreadfort men while spending the levies of other houses — a pattern that raises eyebrows even at the time. Later events suggest this was not merely tactical caution. The Dreadfort foot that survives the Green Fork is the nucleus Bolton uses to hold his position near Harrenhal in the months that follow.

white_harbor_men.name: White Harbor Men
white_harbor_men.description: Twenty-five hundred retainers and household troops of House Manderly of White Harbor — the most southron-influenced house in the North. White Harbor's men are better-armoured than most northern levies, some equipped in the southern style with full mail and heater shields. The city's wealth and maritime connections mean the Manderlys can outfit their soldiers more expensively than most northern lords. Wylis Manderly commands in person. These men form the best-armoured northern contingent, holding the right flank, and they perform creditably before Wylis is captured.
strengths: Best-armoured of the northern units — southern-style equipment provides real defensive advantage
Manderly wealth means these men are paid professionals rather than pure levies
Hold the eastern right flank, which opens onto the best cavalry ground — their defensive posture is correct
High morale from house pride and professional self-image
weaknesses: Tired from the march like everyone else in the northern foot
Opposing Ser Addam Marbrand's heavy cavalry — even the best northern infantry struggles against western knights on open ground
Wylis Manderly is captured in this battle, removing command mid-engagement
white_harbor_men.morale_notes: High morale derived from house pride and professional identity. The White Harbor men consider themselves a cut above the levies. The capture of Wylis is a serious blow to their morale.
white_harbor_men.historical_context: Wylis Manderly (the future Lord Wyman Manderly's son) is captured at the Green Fork along with several other northern officers including Harrion Karstark and others. He is held at Harrenhal until released. The White Harbor contingent represents the most 'southern' military culture in the northern force.

cerwyn_hornwood.name: Cerwyn-Hornwood Levies
cerwyn_hornwood.description: Twenty-five hundred combined levies drawn from House Cerwyn's lands around Cerwyn Castle and House Hornwood's men from the Hornwood itself. These are two mid-tier northern houses whose forces have been amalgamated for the campaign. Lord Medger Cerwyn and Halys Hornwood co-command what is, frankly, the weakest element of the northern force: green troops, lightly equipped, tired, with wavering morale. Their position on the western flank — facing the muddy ground near the Green Fork — is perhaps the best tactical placement for them, since the river bank limits any serious western envelopment. Bolton has placed them where the softest terrain will limit their opponents as much as their own weakness.
strengths: Numerous enough to hold space on the western flank
The muddy ground near the river limits the effectiveness of Lannister cavalry against them
Their presence forces Crakehall's horse to screen defensively rather than threaten the main battle
weaknesses: Wavering morale — these men are not hardened soldiers and they know the situation is bad
Poor equipment and limited training; in a straight fight they lose to comparable Lannister units
Tired from the march and dispirited by the strategic situation
Both Cerwyn and Hornwood become casualties — command disruption at the worst moment
cerwyn_hornwood.morale_notes: Wavering at the start. Any early reverse — a successful cavalry probe, a concentrated arrow volley — may trigger a cascading rout that exposes the western flank. Bolton will not spend political capital to shore them up; they are not his men.
cerwyn_hornwood.historical_context: Lord Medger Cerwyn is severely wounded and later dies of his wounds. Halys Hornwood's fate is also grim — he is killed at the Green Fork or shortly after, and his house loses its lord, setting up the Hornwood inheritance crisis. The Cerwyn-Hornwood levies represent the type of 'other houses' troops that Bolton deliberately feeds into the grinder while preserving his Dreadfort men.

northern_archers.name: Northern Archers
northern_archers.description: Two thousand northern bowmen positioned behind the front line along the Kingsroad axis. Northern archery is competent but not specialized in the way southern crossbow formations are — these are men who hunt as well as fight, capable of sustained fire but lacking the Lannister crossbow's armor-penetrating power at range. They can suppress the Lannister van before contact and continue harassing fire during the engagement. Like all northern units here, they are tired and fighting in a battle they expect to lose.
strengths: Solid pre-contact fire that forces the Lannister van to advance under missile pressure
Northern hunters who understand range estimation and fire discipline
Can engage the Lannister archers on the ridge if positioned on elevated ground near the creek
weaknesses: Tired — reduces accuracy and rate of sustained fire
Positioned behind the front line; if the front collapses the archers are exposed
Lighter bows than Lannister crossbows; less effective against armoured targets at range
Not trained for melee; a cavalry breakthrough reaching them is catastrophic
northern_archers.morale_notes: Steady but tired. These are practical men who do their job without enthusiasm in an engagement they know is unfavourable.
northern_archers.historical_context: The northern archery contingent provides fire support during the engagement but is not a decisive factor. Their main contribution is suppression of the Lannister advance in the early phases of the battle.

northern_light_horse.name: Northern Light Horse
northern_light_horse.description: The approximately one thousand cavalry that Robb left behind with Bolton — scouts, outriders, and light horse. These are not a charging arm; Robb took the heavy cavalry west for the decisive blow at Whispering Wood. What remains are fast movers useful for reconnaissance and screening, positioned in the East Woods to screen the northern right flank and deny Addam Marbrand's horse an easy flanking ride. They cannot stop western knights in open-field combat, but in the woods they can harass and delay.
strengths: Cavalry speed — they can respond to threats across the eastern flank faster than infantry
East Woods terrain negates the Lannister heavy cavalry's advantage
Useful for screening retreats and providing intelligence about Lannister movements
weaknesses: Far too weak to challenge Lannister heavy cavalry on open ground
Tired from the march, even as cavalry
They cannot turn a tactical situation — their role is screening, not fighting
If Marbrand gets around the woods, the light horse cannot stop him
northern_light_horse.morale_notes: Steady in a holding role. These men know their job is delay and screening, not glory. They accept it professionally.
northern_light_horse.historical_context: The pittance of cavalry left with Bolton is one of the clearest expressions of the battle's asymmetry. Robb gambled that Bolton's infantry could fix Tywin without cavalry support — and he was right about the strategic outcome, even if Bolton's tactical situation was dire.

northern_rearguard.name: Northern Rearguard
northern_rearguard.description: The footsore stragglers, late-forming units, and logistical tail of Bolton's force — roughly a thousand men still forming up from the all-night march when the battle begins. These men are physically spent before a blow is struck. Some are lightly wounded from the march; some are simply too exhausted to maintain formation. They represent the inevitable trailing element of any force that has marched through the night to arrive at a surprise engagement. Their military value is near zero; their primary strategic function is to exist as a body that Bolton can evacuate intact as part of his orderly retreat.
strengths: Their existence as a formed body, however weak, provides a nucleus for the eventual retreat
Numbers that occupy space on the deployment map and force the enemy to account for them
weaknesses: Nearly exhausted before fighting begins — their tiredness multiplier devastates their effectiveness
Wavering morale from the combination of exhaustion and the hopeless overall situation
Light infantry without quality equipment
Lowest priority unit on the field; Bolton will not commit his Dreadfort men to save them
northern_rearguard.morale_notes: On the edge of collapse. These men are brave in the northern way — they showed up — but they cannot sustain a fight. A single hard blow will route them.
northern_rearguard.historical_context: Every forced-march attack produces a tail of stragglers. Bolton's all-night march to surprise Tywin was impressive in concept but left approximately a fifth of his force below effective readiness. The rearguard represents this reality. Historically, Bolton manages to withdraw approximately 11,000 of his 16,000 men after the battle — a remarkably high survival rate that suggests these stragglers mostly escape rather than being destroyed.

open.name: Open Ground
open.description: Flat, unobstructed terrain with no natural cover or defensive advantage. Units move freely but cannot shelter.
open.tactical_notes: Cavalry is highly effective on open ground. Infantry is exposed to archery and cavalry charges. No defensive bonus.

plains.name: Open Plains
plains.description: Wide, clear ground offering good visibility and unimpeded movement in all directions.
plains.tactical_notes: The decisive cavalry terrain. Western knights excel here. Northern foot are at a disadvantage against mounted charges in the open. The Center Field is the decisive node — controlling it determines who shapes the battle.

fast_march.name: The Kingsroad
fast_march.description: The maintained road running north-south through the field, enabling rapid troop movement along the axis of advance.
fast_march.tactical_notes: Forces moving along the road gain speed. The Kingsroad is the northern supply axis and line of retreat. Lannister control of the road cuts Bolton's withdrawal options. Northern archers positioned here can fire into the van engagement.

rugged.name: Muddy Ground
rugged.description: The western field near the Green Fork River where poor drainage and river seepage has turned the ground into soft, treacherous footing.
rugged.tactical_notes: Cavalry effectiveness is severely reduced in this terrain. Horses bog down; the lance charge loses its shock value. Lannister left-wing horse is blunted here. Northern Cerwyn-Hornwood foot can hold more effectively than they could on firm ground. Any unit that routes west may find the river at its back.

river_crossing.name: River Obstacle
river_crossing.description: Either the Green Fork River bank (impassable without a ford) or the unnamed creek crossing the center of the field.
river_crossing.tactical_notes: The Green Fork Bank is effectively impassable — it anchors the western flank of both armies. The Creek is crossable but disorders units in the process, reducing their combat effectiveness on arrival at the far bank. Units crossing the creek during an advance take a coordination penalty.

ambush.name: East Woods
ambush.description: A belt of light woodland on the far eastern flank, providing broken sightlines and cover for cavalry screening operations.
ambush.tactical_notes: Northern light horse in the East Woods can negate Lannister heavy cavalry's open-ground superiority. The woods limit the western knights' ability to swing wide around the northern right flank. Any Lannister attempt to use the east woods as an outflanking route is slowed and potentially intercepted.

easy_defend.name: Tywin's Ridge
easy_defend.description: A low but militarily significant ridge to the south of the main battle, commanding the field and providing the Lannister army its prepared reserve position.
easy_defend.tactical_notes: Defenders on the ridge gain elevation advantage for archery and have downhill momentum for cavalry charges. The Lannister crossbows here suppress the northern advance from a position of relative safety. Tywin's reserve launches its decisive charge from this ground. If northern forces reach the ridge, they have effectively broken the Lannister army.

capital_lannister.name: Lannister Command Position
capital_lannister.description: Tywin Lannister's command post and the anchor of the Lannister reserve deployment — the strategic heart of the western force.
capital_lannister.tactical_notes: Tywin directs the battle from this position with cold patience. The ridge is the Lannister 'last stand' node. If northern forces break through to seize it, the battle is over. The reserve horse is committed from here at the decisive moment. Losing this node = losing the battle for the Lannisters.

capital_stark.name: Stark Muster Point
capital_stark.description: The northern army's entry and muster point on the Kingsroad, the farthest north node and the point from which Bolton's force advanced.
capital_stark.tactical_notes: The northern rear area. Dreadfort foot and the rearguard stragglers form up here. If Lannister forces drive this far north, the northern army has been routed. Bolton's orderly retreat aims to preserve a viable force that can regroup here. Losing this position = total northern collapse.

assault.description: Full-speed aggressive attack with maximum offensive commitment. Units close rapidly and hit hard, accepting casualties to maximize shock.
assault.tactical_notes: Tywin's reserve horse should assault when the northern line is spent. The mountain clans fight best on assault — it matches their charge-oriented style. Assaulting against a dug-in position on the ridge is costly; save assault for broken or tired targets.
assault.game_effect: Significant attack bonus, defense penalty. Best used by fresh heavy cavalry against exhausted infantry.

attack.description: Coordinated offensive action with maintained cohesion and some defensive awareness.
attack.tactical_notes: The standard combat order for most units. Northern vanguard spears should attack the van line. Lannister center should attack to counter-push once the northern assault loses momentum.

breakthrough.description: Offensive drive aimed at punching through the enemy line and penetrating to the rear, accepting flanking risk.
breakthrough.tactical_notes: A breakthrough by the northern vanguard through the van line could reach the ridge and threaten the Lannister archers and reserve. High risk, high reward. Tywin's reserve should not need breakthrough — assault delivers sufficient shock.
breakthrough.game_effect: High attack bonus, no defensive bonus. Unit may advance through a defeated node. Flanking risk.

defend.description: Hold position with full defensive formation. Accept combat as defender rather than attacking.
defend.tactical_notes: Lannister vanguard foot in the van line should fight defensively — their job is to absorb the northern charge, not to deliver one. Northern archers on the Kingsroad should defend if threatened. The western levies defending buys them survival time when they might otherwise route.

dig_in.description: Establish fieldworks and defensive preparations at the current position.
dig_in.tactical_notes: Lannister archers on the ridge should dig in for maximum archery protection. Digging in at Center Field creates a defensible anchor if the northern attack is repulsed and Bolton wants to hold ground. Tywin's center men-at-arms digging in turns the battle into a grinding northern attrition — Bolton cannot afford that.

hold.description: Maintain position without advancing or withdrawing, prepared to fight if attacked.
hold.tactical_notes: Dreadfort foot should hold in the rear until Bolton decides to commit or withdraw. Left wing horse holds the river flank. Holding is Bolton's strategic posture for his best troops.
hold.game_effect: No movement. Defensive bonus if attacked. Sets up orderly withdrawal options.

deny.description: Block enemy movement through a node by digging in and threatening intercept fire.
deny.tactical_notes: Lannister archers on the ridge deny the ridge approach from the van line — any northern unit moving to the ridge without first clearing the archers takes significant fire. Northern archers on the Kingsroad can deny the road axis.
deny.game_effect: Units attempting to pass through or engage the denying unit take intercept fire. Effectiveness depends on dig-in level.

reinforce.description: Move to support adjacent friendly units without triggering a primary engagement.
reinforce.tactical_notes: Bolton reinforcing the van with Dreadfort foot is a major decision — it commits his best unit to the grinder. Tywin reinforcing the van line from the center is risky because it delays the reserve timing. Best used to shore up a failing flank before the position collapses.

retreat.description: Withdraw from contact toward friendly rear areas.
retreat.tactical_notes: Bolton's signature move — the orderly retreat that preserves the northern force for later operations. Northern units retreating north along the Kingsroad have a clear withdrawal axis. Retreating over the creek while under pressure takes casualties. Lannister pursuit after a northern retreat is where their cavalry advantage becomes devastating.

cover.description: Provide fire or position support to protect a withdrawing or exposed friendly unit.
cover.tactical_notes: Dreadfort foot covering the withdrawal of the spent northern van is exactly the kind of professional use Bolton makes of his troops. Northern archers covering the retreat of the vanguard spears can blunt Lannister pursuit.

disengage.description: Both sides agree to cease combat in a node and separate their forces.
disengage.tactical_notes: Disengage is relevant when Bolton decides the engagement has served its purpose — he has fixed Tywin long enough — and needs to extract his force. A mutual disengage at the van line would allow Bolton to withdraw in order. Tywin is unlikely to consent; his cavalry can exploit a northern retreat.

flanked.description: A unit has been attacked from an unexpected direction, suffering serious cohesion penalties.
flanked.tactical_notes: The northern force is critically vulnerable to flanking by Tywin's reserve horse descending from the ridge. If the reserve hits a van unit already engaged frontally, the flanked condition is catastrophic — it is the historical 'shatter like glass' moment. Lannister left wing horse flanking the Cerwyn-Hornwood levies from the west could trigger a cascade collapse of the northern left.
